mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 2 Series 230i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 2 Series 230i engine replacement typically costs between £2,200 and £3,800 depending on the condition (used, reconditioned, or rebuilt). Used engines start from around £1,500, reconditioned units from £2,200, and fully rebuilt engines with a 12-month warranty from £2,800. Labour for supply and fit adds approximately £800-£1,500 depending on the workshop. Main dealer replacement costs can exceed £4,500.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 2 Series 230i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning sign is a metallic rattling noise from the engine on cold start, which typically lasts 2-5 seconds before disappearing as oil pressure builds. BMW issued Service Bulletin SI B11 01 18 confirming timing chain guide degradation as a known weakness in B48 engines. Other symptoms include a metallic ticking sound, engine hesitation, and in severe cases, the engine management light illuminating with fault codes P000A, P0016, or P0017.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 2 Series 230i?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's value and the extent of the damage. For a 230i worth £20,000-£30,000 (typical for 2021-2023 models), replacement is almost always justified. If the car is worth under £5,000, a used engine or repair may be more cost-effective. Given the relatively high value of most 230i examples, a rebuilt engine with a 12-month warranty is often the most sensible long-term investment.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 2 Series 230i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 2 Series 230i engine replacement takes 3-5 working days from order to completion, assuming the engine is in stock. Supply-only orders are usually dispatched within 1-2 working days. Supply and fit through our specialist network typically takes 3-5 days, including delivery, fitting, and ECU calibration.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the 230i and the 220i engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW 230i uses a high-output 2.0-litre B48B20O1 engine producing 245hp and 400Nm of torque, while the 220i uses a lower-output version of the same B48 family producing 181-184hp. The 230i offers significantly more power and torque, with a 0-62mph time of 5.7-5.9 seconds compared to 7.3 seconds for the 220i.

mainEntity.name: Will a replacement BMW 2 Series 230i engine pass the MoT?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - all engines supplied through EnginesMarket are MoT emissions compliant. Rebuilt and reconditioned engines are tested to ensure they meet the original emissions standards for the vehicle's year. For 230i models with OPF (Otto Particulate Filter), compliance is confirmed before dispatch.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 2 Series 230i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 2 Series 230i is powered by the B48B20O1 2.0-litre four-cylinder turbo petrol engine - part of BMW's modular B-series engine family. While generally reliable, the B48 has a few well-documented weaknesses including timing chain tensioner wear, oil filter housing cracking, and coolant system leaks. BMW acknowledged the timing chain defect and issued Service Bulletin SI B11 01 18. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Why the BMW 2 Series 230i B48 Engine Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The B48 uses a single-row timing chain system that has proven prone to premature stretch and guide wear. Unlike older multi-row chains, this design relies on a plastic tensioner rail that degrades faster under heat stress - especially in stop-start urban driving. When the chain stretches beyond tolerance, it can skip teeth on the camshaft sprocket, throwing off valve timing and leading to valve-piston collision. BMW acknowledged the defect and issued Service Bulletin SI B11 01 18 confirming timing chain guide degradation as a known weakness.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace chain, guides, tensioner, VANOS units
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if rattle is persistent or mileage >70k

If you hear a metallic rattle on cold start lasting 2-5 seconds, have the car inspected immediately. A full timing chain kit replacement with upgraded components is the most cost-effective long-term solution. Given the high value of most 230i examples, a rebuilt engine with a 12-month warranty is often the most sensible long-term investment.

problems.h4: Oil Filter Housing Cracking - BMW 2 Series 230i Coolant and Oil Leaks
problems.rootCause: The B48 oil filter housing is made of plastic and can crack over time, creating coolant or oil leaks. Because the housing is located underneath the intake manifold, the manifold must be removed to access it, making repairs labour-intensive. Dealership costs for this repair can be substantial.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove intake manifold, replace housing and gaskets
repairOptions.longevity: Effective; upgraded units typically don't fail again

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Pressure test, inspect for additional leaks

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a typical £20,000-£30,000 230i, oil filter housing replacement is a worthwhile repair. Full engine replacement is rarely needed for this failure alone, though coolant loss from a cracked housing can lead to overheating and secondary damage if ignored.
problems.recommendation: Oil filter housing cracking is a known issue on B48 engines. Regularly check for coolant or oil puddles under the car. If you notice a sweet smell or visible leaks, have the housing inspected promptly. Replacing the housing with an upgraded unit typically solves the problem permanently.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for BMW 2 Series 230i oil filter housing repair

problems.h4: Coolant System Failures - BMW 2 Series 230i Overheating and Coolant Loss
problems.rootCause: The B48 cooling system uses plastic components that can degrade under heat stress. The electric water pump and coolant return line hose are known failure points. Coolant leaks can lead to overheating and, in severe cases, head gasket failure.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a typical £20,000-£30,000 230i, cooling system repairs are minor expenses relative to vehicle value. Full engine replacement is rarely needed for cooling system failure alone, unless overheating has caused head gasket or piston damage.
problems.recommendation: Cooling system issues are common on B48 engines. Regularly check coolant levels and inspect for visible leaks. If you notice a sweet smell or coolant puddles, have the system inspected promptly.
